summary: Evaluate the specified local Mikkelsen mathematical heating-partition approximation, including its finite zero-energy limit.

capability: Local Mikkelsen approximation for the fast-ion heating fraction including its finite zero-energy limit.
operation: birth energy, electron temperature and fast ion mass -> ion heating fraction
discovery.model: Specified local Mikkelsen approximation with fixed x^2 = E_birth/(10 m_fast T_e) scaling.
discovery.geometry: Local homogeneous plasma; scalar or broadcast array values with no spatial geometry.
discovery.boundary: E_birth >= 0, T_e > 0 and fast-ion mass > 0, all finite.

identity.relation: f_i(x)=2/x² integral from 0 to x of t/(1+t³) dt, x²=E_birth/(10 m_fast T_e)
identity.direction: birth energy, electron temperature and fast ion mass -> ion heating fraction
identity.definition: The dimensionless Mikkelsen partition is evaluated by a convergent small-x series and its closed form away from zero; f_i(0)=1 is the continuous limit.
identity.model: Specified local Mikkelsen approximation with fixed x²=E_birth/(10 m_fast T_e) scaling
identity.geometry: local homogeneous plasma; no spatial geometry input
identity.boundary: E_birth >= 0, T_e > 0, fast-ion mass > 0; all finite
assumptions: T_e is in keV and fast-ion mass is in atomic mass units.
The relation is a local partition and does not model slowing-down trajectories.
The fixed scaling defines the evaluated approximation; suitability for a specific plasma composition or collisional regime is not established by numerical agreement with this relation.

inputs.name: fast_ion_mass
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; broadcast-compatible with the other inputs.

outputs.name: ion_fraction
outputs.description: Fraction of fast-ion heating deposited into ions

preconditions: All declared inputs satisfy the finite domain and broadcast compatibility.
supported: Numerical evaluation of the exact dimensionless integral and fixed energy/temperature/mass scaling stated in this document.
excluded: Negative birth energy, nonpositive temperature or mass, nonfinite values, and full transport or trajectory evolution.
Claims of experimental calibration or suitability for arbitrary plasma compositions and collisional regimes.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for nonfinite, out-of-domain or broadcast-incompatible inputs; raises FloatingPointError when the computed dimensionless ratio or result is nonfinite, including ratio overflow from finite dimensional inputs.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Propagates numerical failures; no fallback or clipping is applied.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the small-x series has fixed 12-term order.

example.description: Evaluate the zero-energy boundary and a finite energy case.
example.code:
from scirel.plasma.fast_ion_heating import fast_ion_fractional_heating
assert fast_ion_fractional_heating(0.0, 10.0, 2.0) == 1.0
value = fast_ion_fractional_heating(20.0, 4.0, 2.0)
assert 0.0 < value < 1.0
example.expected: The zero-energy limit is exactly 1 and the finite case returns a finite dimensionless fraction.

scope: Independent integral quadrature and continuous zero-energy limit.
Closed-form agreement at a held-out finite energy.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Independent quadrature, analytic boundary limits and regression tests support numerical evaluation of the stated mathematical relation under the declared failure behavior. They do not establish experimental calibration or wider physical applicability.
known_limitations: Numerical verification establishes evaluation of the specified mathematical approximation, not experimental calibration or applicability to a particular plasma composition or collisional regime.
Finite input values can produce a nonfinite dimensionless ratio and then raise FloatingPointError.
Full slowing-down trajectories, spatial transport evolution and coupling to other plasma models are outside this operator.

references: Mikkelsen, Nucl. Technol. Fusion 237 (1983), equations 5 and 26
